q.t: In a pictograph, 1 teddy picture = 5 toys. There are 8 pictures. How many toys?
q.e: Reading a pictograph is multiplying: 8 pictures × 5 toys each.

q.t: What does a pictograph tell you if its key is missing?
o: Nothing exact — each picture could stand for any number
Exactly how many things there are
q.e: The key turns pictures into numbers. Without it, 8 pictures could mean 8, 40 or 800.

q.t: 1 picture = 10 books. What does HALF a picture stand for?
q.e: Half of 10 is 5.

q.t: 1 picture = 10 books. A row has 3 whole pictures and a half picture. How many books?
q.e: 30 for the whole pictures and 5 for the half.

q.t: In a bar graph, what does the HEIGHT of a bar show?
q.e: The bar’s height is read off the scale up the side.

q.t: Every bar in a bar graph should start at:
q.e: We compare heights, so a bar starting higher up would look shorter than it really is.

q.t: In a TV survey, 4, 9, 11, 7 and 4 children chose the five groups. How many children in all?
q.e: Add the groups. They should add back to the number of children asked.

q.t: 1 picture = 2 children. A row has 6 pictures. How many children?
q.e: 6 pictures × 2 children each.

q.t: 1 picture = 5 toys. How many pictures do you draw for 40 toys?
q.e: Drawing a pictograph is dividing: 40 ÷ 5 = 8.

q.t: Food wasted: Monday 4 kg, Tuesday 6 kg, Wednesday 8 kg, Thursday 3 kg. On which day was the MOST wasted?
q.e: 8 kg is the biggest number in the table.

q.t: Food wasted in a week: 4 kg, 6 kg, 8 kg, 3 kg and 5 kg. What is the total?
q.e: Add all five days.

q.t: Food wasted: Mon 4 kg, Tue 6 kg, Wed 8 kg, Thu 3 kg, Fri 5 kg. On which day was the LEAST wasted?
q.e: 3 kg is the smallest number.

q.t: 1 picture = 3 two-wheelers. Monday has 7 pictures. How many two-wheelers?
Monday had 21 two-wheelers and Wednesday had 12. How many fewer on Wednesday?
q.e: ‘How many fewer’ means find the difference.

q.t: TV hours: 1/2 hour — 4 children, 1 hour — 9, 1 1/2 hours — 11, 2 hours — 7, more than 2 hours — 4. How many watch LESS THAN 2 hours?
q.e: Less than 2 leaves out the 2-hour group: 4 + 9 + 11.

q.t: Same TV table. How many watch MORE than half an hour?
q.e: Leave out only the 1/2-hour group: 9 + 11 + 7 + 4.

q.t: Same TV table. How many watch AT MOST 2 hours?
q.e: ‘At most 2’ includes the 2-hour group: 4 + 9 + 11 + 7.

q.t: The data are 40, 25 and 30. Which scale (1 picture = ?) shows them all with whole pictures and not too many?
q.e: 5 divides 40, 25 and 30 exactly (8, 5 and 6 pictures). 1 would need 95 pictures; 3 and 50 don’t divide them.

q.t: 7 out of 15 children wear glasses. Is that more than half?
o: No — half of 15 is 7 1/2, and 7 is less
q.e: ‘More than half’ needs counting, not a guess.

q.t: How can you show that ‘All the girls wear glasses’ is FALSE?
q.e: ‘All’ means every single one, so one exception is enough.

q.t: 1 picture = 4 books. A row shows 5 1/2 pictures. How many books?
q.e: 5 × 4 = 20, and half a picture is half of 4 = 2.

q.t: 1 picture = 4 cars. How many pictures show 18 cars?
q.e: 4 pictures show 16 cars, and the last 2 cars are half a picture.

q.t: With 1 picture = 3, why can’t you show 20?
o: 20 is not a multiple of 3, and half a picture would be 1 1/2
q.e: 6 pictures = 18 and 7 = 21, and half a picture means 1 1/2 things.

q.t: 26 kg of food was wasted. If 1 kg can feed 3 children, how many children could have been fed?
q.e: 26 × 3 = 78 — the number becomes a reason to waste less.

q.t: Sheela’s day: sleep 9 hr, school 6 hr, study 2 hr, eating and play 4 hr, and other things. How many hours for other things?
q.e: A day has 24 hours, so the parts must add up to 24.

q.t: Two-wheelers: Monday 21, Wednesday 12, Friday 18. What is the total?
q.e: Add all three days.

q.t: Two-wheelers: Wednesday 12, Friday 18. How many more on Friday?
q.e: Difference = 18 − 12.

q.t: Khichdi was wasted most this week. What is the best way to say what will happen next week?
o: Khichdi will LIKELY be wasted most
Nothing can be guessed at all
q.e: One week of data is a hint, not a certainty — say ‘likely’.

q.t: To show that ‘Some children wear caps’ is FALSE, you must:
o: Check every child and find none with a cap
Find one child without a cap
Find one child with a cap
q.e: ‘Some’ means at least one, so you must check them all.

q.t: Before comparing bars on two different bar graphs, what must you check first?
o: That both use the same scale
That the bars are the same colour
q.e: On a different scale, a shorter bar can stand for a bigger number.

q.t: 1 picture = 10 fruits. Apples: 6 1/2 pictures, bananas: 9 pictures, mangoes: 4 pictures. How many fruits in all?
q.e: Apples 65, bananas 90, mangoes 40. 65 + 90 + 40 = 195.

q.t: Same pictograph: how many MORE bananas than mangoes?
q.e: 9 − 4 = 5 more pictures, and 5 × 10 = 50.

q.t: The data are 12, 18, 30 and 24. Which scale shows ALL of them with whole pictures?
q.e: 6 divides all four (2, 3, 5, 4 pictures). 4 and 12 don’t divide 18; 5 doesn’t divide 12.

q.t: 40 children choose a favourite game: cricket 15, football 9, kabaddi 6, and the rest chess. How many chose chess?
q.e: The groups must add back to 40: 40 − 30 = 10.

q.t: Same survey: 15 of the 40 chose cricket. How many MORE would need to choose cricket for it to be more than half?
q.e: Half of 40 is 20, so more than half needs at least 21. 21 − 15 = 6.

q.t: Library books: 1 picture = 8 books. Monday shows 3 1/2 pictures, Tuesday 5 pictures. How many books on the two days?
On Ravi’s graph 1 square = 1 hour, and his study bar is 2 squares tall. On Meena’s graph 1 square = 2 hours, and her study bar is 3 squares tall. How many more hours does Meena study?
q.e: Ravi: 2 × 1 = 2 hours. Meena: 3 × 2 = 6 hours. Compare the numbers, not the bars.

q.t: A canteen wasted 26 kg in a week of 5 days. If it wastes 2 kg less EACH day, what is the new weekly total?
q.e: 2 kg less on each of 5 days is 10 kg less: 26 − 10.

q.t: 1 picture = 10, and half pictures are allowed. Which number CANNOT be shown?
q.e: Half a picture is 5, so only multiples of 5 can be shown.

q.t: Water used each day of a week (litres): 120, 135, 150, 125, 140, 160, 130. On how many days was it MORE than 135?
q.e: 150, 140 and 160. 135 itself is not MORE than 135.
